text: Bhuvaneshwar Prasad Sinha [Title: Sinha] of Shahabad (now Bhojpur), Bengal Presidency (1 February 1899 – 12 November 1986) was the 6th Chief Justice of India, serving from 1 October 1959 to 31 January 1964. He also served as the president of the Bharat Scouts and Guides from April 1965 to February 1967. Sinha served as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India from 1 October 1959 to 31 January 1964, during which he authored 137 judgments and sat on 684 benches. Born and raised in a prominent Rajput (Kshatriya) family of Rajwada Gajiyapur Estate, Arrah (present Bhojpur) District, his grandson B. P. Singh is a former judge of the Supreme Court of India. A deeply religious man, Sinha led a quiet life after retirement, mostly devoted to spiritual pursuits, though he accepted a number of private arbitration cases. Becoming blind in his later years, he died in 1986. He was educated at the Arrah Zilla School, Patna College, and Patna Law College. Sinha topped the list of candidates at the B.A. (Hons) in 1919 and M.A in 1921 at Patna University. He was a Vakil in the Patna High Court from 1922 to 1927, became an advocate in 1927, and served as Lecturer at the Govt. Law College, Patna, holding both positions until 1935. He was also a member of the Senate of the Faculty of Law and of the Board of Examiners in Law at Patna University and a member of the Court of Benaras Hindu University as a Government Pleader from 1935 to 1939, where he was a Srimati Radhika Sinha Gold Medalist for standing first in History. He became an Assistant Govt. Advocate in 1940 and was appointed Judge of the Patna High Court on 19 January 1943. He was elevated to Chief Justice of the Nagpur High Court in 1951 and later became a Judge of the Supreme Court in December 1954, serving until 30 September 1959. He was then appointed Chief Justice of India in 1959 and remained in office until 1964, after which he retired.
